head: fc3f2814
gate: HTTP/3 ConcurrentStream.startResponseWithBody submits the response head and first DATA contribution as one owner command
problem: A sequential request paid two owner round trips: the handler blocked on start_response, then blocked again on write_body. Command tracing had shown each round trip costs roughly the wake plus Select cycle, which dominated the 76-101 us sequential latency even though the owner's send itself took only 5-25 us.
change: New additive API `ConcurrentStream.startResponseWithBody(response, body_length, data, fin)` plus a deadline form. The owner executes the head and the first body contribution in one command. HEAD/204/304 still suppress the body: non-empty data is rejected as InvalidContentLength and fin marks the response finished. `startResponse`/`writeData` keep their existing semantics.

benchmark.workload: netz-only harness (zio event loop, HandshakeServer.serveConcurrentStreams + client startRequest/receiveNextResponse), GET / -> 200 "ok"

notes: Sequential dropped 101.8 -> 59.2 us/request in the netz harness and batch=8 dropped 53.2 -> 39.7 us/request. batch=32 is unchanged within noise because its latency is dominated by per-packet work, not by one extra command round trip. Weft must call the new method to see the win; the existing startResponse/writeData sequence keeps its current cost. The new test covers the ordinary GET path and HEAD suppression is already covered by the existing suppress-body tests.
